searchText: Hi all, I have been reading several EIPs and noticed the references to other EIPs aren't anchor tags. Is that by design? If not, is it worth discussing adding those for a better user experience going forward and having a story to revisit prior releases and edit them? <@!204403053233700869> per EIP-1 it's required to hyperlink to the eip the first time it's mentioned. I think we do an okay job of enforcing this, but sometimes things slip through and older EIPs may not respect this. <@!642887713246150666> regarding https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/4329 there's a very long standing debate https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/issues/1121. If you want to go through and add links to all that are missing I would support such work. I’m thinking of a commit lifecycle filter that would automatically convert the EIP mentions to anchor tags. What do folks think? I see. Makes sense. What is a commit lifecycle filter? Like a piece of code that runs to check if there are any mentions of EIP and replace them with the hyperlink at commit time Most editors use the GitHub interface, which means precommit hooks won't run. Hmmm. I think there is some opportunity to have server side validators run but that may be too much work for something so small hahah Yeah, almost certainly not worth the maintenance effort. To be fair it is fairly simple, due to git history: `git checkout 491e7f5fe` gives you back the version from Berlin (the one you withdrew). Did it here for convenience: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/4331 Ah! I see. Comments there makes it unclear to me, if people actually don't like this proposal getting into final or some changes needs to be done to make it even better. I see Ricmoo talking about "backwards compatibility note", but as I understand it's up to the author to accept or reject suggestions. (I may be wrong though.) The main dispute was that people like the proposal, and would like it to be adopted, but the specification makes that not possible, because it stipulates which chain id has it turned on. Once it turns final, the EIP can't be changed to have it adopted by other chains -- at least that is the debate. At this point also there's a meta question: the format of it doesn't match the current requirements. On that note it cannot be finalised, however given the review period ran out way earlier, does that mean the rules at that time apply to it? The author has put into significant work and the proposal is in the Last Call for over a year and would be better to see it as a standard for Ethereum. Anything that we can do help move in the right direction will be helpful. > the format of it doesn't match the current requirements. This is a bigger concern. Technically it won't be a standard for mainnet, because mainnet can only adopt it if the text is changed post-finalization 🙂 As it stands currently, if moved to final, it will only ever be a standard for rootstock. Interesting! Would love to hear more thoughts on it. Any suggestions for adding a status to address such proposal(s)? It says `if a registered chain id is provided,`, but doesn't specify where this register lives and how to register it. And the implementation section (which is not a valid section anymore) hardcodes this decision of "registered". To summarise: the long standing debate for over 2 years has been about these meta questions. As far as I've seen ecosystem tooling people complained about this (ethers.js, hardhat), and their concerns were not addressed, so not sure if it will be adopted given that. Here's the thread from hardhat: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2143 What status do you mean? Thanks for sharing this link. I will reach the author to check if she is aware of any adoption for this proposal at all. Because there is a mention of adoption but not clear which project. If you read all the comments, the conversation is not that amicable. I think this is a subjective decision about usefulness. If we care about usefulness of final EIPs, then it would be important to guide authors to make sure their EIP is as useful as possible, in this case that means it is easily adoptable without the need to change the EIP text at every single occasion. If we want to avoid this hurdle of subjective judging, then once an EIP fulfils the technical requirements, it should be allowed to progress to final, despite to various concerns/disagreements. It just means people can fork the EIP and create a new one which they deem is better. As I understood that if an author wants to move it's proposal without accepting suggestions during the review period, he/she is free to do so and there can always be another proposal which can improve the existing "Final" standard. I was wondering if we run into case where an EIP can go to Final because it is technically correct but may not be considered as a standard because the format is obsolete or doesn't match the current mainnet, should there be a unique status for such proposals? (Given "Supersede" is not a status any more) I would agree. There are fine lines and I am trying to document them for future reference as this is not formally added in the EIP-1. https://hackmd.io/@poojaranjan/EIP-ERC-Editor-handbook#Exceptional-cases Happy to make changes depending on decisions made by EIP editors. ' I take that as a strong suggestion that I should replace my current edit 2315 with a new Draft. I'll consider it, thanks for making it easier.
